detail.body: RFC: #62100 ## Purpose Follow-up to #42309. vLLM picks the KV cache grouping of every model with one heuristic in core (`get_kv_cache_groups()`). New hybrid models, drafters, cache precisions and platforms keep needing plans that this heuristic does not give, so each new model changes core, and vllm-ascend monkey-patches core planning to use its own DSV4 plan. This PR adds an **experimental** pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder`. Core keeps one planning flow and checks every plan. A platform selects a builder that decides grouping and placement, and a model can return its own groups. The interfaces can change, in particular when #61452 changes the KV cache group data structure. ## Changes - **`KVCacheConfigBuilder`** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_config_builder.py`) with two decisions: `get_kv_cache_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec)` and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)`. A platform selects the class with `Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`; the default is `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`. - **Core owns the planning flow.** `get_kv_cache_configs` is a core function, not a builder method: merge specs, group, check, project onto PP stages, apply the block-count override, auto-fit and admission, place, and converge ranks. Platforms make only the two decisions above. - **Bytes per block come from the builder's placement.** Core places one block and reads its single device backing, so a platform with its own placement does not compute memory separately. A placement with several device allocations overrides the private, transitional `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` (until worker-driven allocation, #42449). - **Model-owned grouping.** A model class can implement `SupportsKVCacheGrouping.get_kv_cache_groups` (a classmethod). Priority: a platform builder that overrides grouping (it reaches the model hook only through `super()`), then the model hook, then the default heuristic. - **Every grouping is checked**, from any source, on the planning path and both profiling paths: each layer is in exactly one group. - **Profiling** passes `num_blocks` directly instead of temporarily setting `num_gpu_blocks_override`. Bug fixes: - PP projection now keeps `host_resident`, `role` and `enable_kv_transfer` on partially projected groups. - `num_gpu_blocks_override` no longer inflates the one-block probe (it gave `500 * C` instead of `C` bytes per block). - HiSparse keeps the direct bytes computation, because probing its placement would size the host pool before auto-fit. A model hook combined with HiSparse raises a clear error. ## Users - vllm-ascend#18359 moves the Ascend plans into an `AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder` and removes most of its planning patches. - wangxiyuan/vllm#2 (stacked on this PR): model hooks for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Kimi-K3 (Kimi-K3 + DSpark: 5 groups instead of 20), and golden grouping plans per model. Not a duplicate: #58638 (#58207, #58380) improves the default heuristic for drafters. That work is complementary; this PR adds the extension point and does not change the default grouping. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py ``` ## Test Result 83 passed (head `6283b0aca3`, GB200 node). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. The authors reviewed every changed line. Co-Authored-By: Yifan Qiao Co-Authored-By: Mengqing Cao Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Interface and resolution for pluggable KV cache config builders."""
+
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import resolve_obj_by_qualname
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+        KVCacheConfig,
+        KVCacheGroupSpec,
+        KVCacheSpec,
+    )
+
+
+class KVCacheConfigBuilder(ABC):
+    """Interface for platform KV cache placement.
+
+    .. note::
+        This interface is experimental and subject to change. The exact hooks
+        and the ``num_blocks`` contract may evolve before it stabilizes.
+
+    Subclasses normally inherit from ``DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`` and
+    override only the hooks they need. The cross-worker planning flow
+    (:func:`vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning.get_kv_cache_configs`) is Core-owned;
+    this builder supplies the placement decisions: how layers are split into
+    groups and how a group list is materialized into tensors for a given block
+    count. Grouping coordination lives in ``DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`` (a
+    model implementing :class:`~vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces.
+    SupportsKVCacheGrouping` owns its grouping there); a platform that replaces
+    the builder fully owns its own grouping.
+    """
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_kv_cache_groups(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_spec: dict[str, "KVCacheSpec"],
+    ) -> list["KVCacheGroupSpec"]:
+        """Split the given layers into KV cache groups.
+
+        Planning passes all workers' layers; profiling passes one worker's.
+        Core rejects a result that does not put each layer in exactly one group.
+
+        The default builder honors a model's
+        :class:`~vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces.SupportsKVCacheGrouping`
+        declaration here before falling back to the default grouping; a
+        platform-specific builder decides its own grouping.
+        """
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_groups: list["KVCacheGroupSpec"],
+        num_blocks: int,
+    ) -> "KVCacheConfig":
+        """Materialize the groups for exactly ``num_blocks`` blocks.
+
+        Each device backing's size is ``bytes_per_block * num_blocks``. All
+        device tensors share one backing allocation unless the builder
+        overrides ``_get_pool_bytes_per_block``. Host-resident tensors, such as
+        HiSparse source storage, are excluded from the device byte accounting
+        and sized independently.
+        """
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def _get_pool_bytes_per_block(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_groups: list["KVCacheGroupSpec"],
+    ) -> int | None:
+        """Return the device bytes one block ID consumes, or ``None``.
+
+        Private and transitional; expected to go away with worker-driven
+        allocation (RFC #42449). With ``None`` (the default), Core derives the
+        value from a one-block placement with one device backing. Override it
+        only for placements with several device allocations.
+        """
+        return None
+
+
+def get_kv_cache_config_builder(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+) -> KVCacheConfigBuilder:
+    """Resolve the builder selected by the current platform.
+
+    Resolution priority is owned by the platform hook
+    (:meth:`vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`).
+    Builders are stateless (every method takes ``vllm_config``), so a fresh
+    instance is returned per call and engines with different configs in the
+    same process always get the correct builder.
+    """
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    builder_cls = resolve_obj_by_qualname(
+        current_platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls(vllm_config)
+    )
+    return builder_cls()

+def _pool_bytes_per_block_from_builder(
+    builder: KVCacheConfigBuilder,
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    kv_cache_groups: list[KVCacheGroupSpec],
+) -> int:
+    """Bytes consumed by one block in the worker's device KV cache pool.
+
+    Core places one block with the builder and reads the size of its single
+    device backing. A placement with several device allocations declares the
+    value through ``KVCacheConfigBuilder._get_pool_bytes_per_block``. HiSparse
+    keeps the pure computation, since probing its placement would check the host
+    pool against ``max_model_len`` before auto-fit shortens it.
+    ``num_gpu_blocks_override`` is suppressed so it cannot inflate the probe.
+    """
+    if not kv_cache_groups:
+        return 0

Refactoring the previous `get_kv_cache_configs()` into smaller APIs seems like a good direction. I wonder if the public interface could be simplified further.

My understanding is that most of the current methods can be put into common core codes. Layout validation, memory admission checks, `num_gpu_blocks_override`, auto-fit, null-block reservation, and cross-rank alignment could remain internal to Core. 

Profiling also does not seem to require a separate API. It already knows the min block count. For final allocation, the current GPU backing size is linear in `num_blocks`, so Core can ask the placement hook to describe a hypothetical one-block pool, without allocating GPU memory, and use that backing size to derive the final block count from `available_memory`. This also removes the need for `get_pool_bytes_per_block()`. 

The public interface could therefore be reduced to `get_kv_cache_configs()` as the full-flow escape hatch, plus `get_kv_cache_groups()` for logical grouping and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(..., num_blocks)` for physical placement. Platforms with a non-linear capacity model could still override the top-level flow.

I made a small prototype here: https://github.com/andakai/vllm/compare/refactor/pr53558-main-baseline...refactor/pr53558-public-api-simplification. I may have missed some platform-specific requirements and whether this smaller interface makes sense.
